result.title: Monitorability Is Trainable: Post-Training for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
result.comment: The first two authors contributed equally
result.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is one of the few practical tools available for overseeing capable AI systems, but it is fragile: a model's reasoning is only useful to a monitor if it remains coupled to what the model actually does. This coupling can be degraded during training through, for example, CoT compression, optimization against a monitor, and out-of-context generalization from synthetic documents. In this work, we propose an unsupervised post-training objective based on maximizing mutual information between CoT and the output for improving CoT monitorability. Across three model organisms with degraded CoT, it recovers most or all of the lost monitorability. Applied to undegraded policies, it further improves judged monitorability, improves prediction of unsafe behavior by CoT monitors and activation probes, and increases the prevalence of consequential reasoning. These results suggest that monitorability should be treated as a trainable attribute of the policy. A dedicated monitorability post-training stage can extend current practices that protect CoT from direct optimization pressure.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一种无监督后训练目标，通过最大化 CoT 与最终输出之间的互信息来提升 CoT 的可监控性，并在三个 CoT 已被压损的模型与未退化策略上验证其能恢复或进一步提升可监控性、改善对不安全行为的预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「让推理轨迹与输出保持互信息耦合」的训练目标，可能为 LVR 中「答案是否真正使用内部推理内容」这一问题提供可核查的监督与贡献分配线索，但论文面向纯文本 CoT，非视觉或多模态状态。
